title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 4: not optimum — strips pure mercy; Detur totum Deo; Cyprian
pass_a_gloss: Solution. That God does all things in the best mode, no one except the worst dares deny: but we deny nonetheless that the best mode of electing men to eternal life is that which rests on foresight of merits. It is not the best, because it does not best serve to illustrate the glory of the pure divine mercy toward the elect. For it takes away that which Augustine everywhere inculcates, Let the whole be given to God. It also takes away that of Cyprian, never enough praised by Augustine, In nothing is one to glory; because nothing is ours.
pass_b_english: Sol. That God does all things in the best way no one but the worst would deny — yet we deny that the best way of electing people to eternal life is the one that rests on foresight of merits. It is not best, because it does least to display the glory of God’s pure mercy toward the elect. It strips what Augustine everywhere presses: Let the whole be given to God. It also strips Cyprian’s line, which Augustine never praised enough: In nothing is one to glory, because nothing is ours.
source_text: Sol. Deum optimo modo omnia facere, nemo nisi pessimus audet negare: sed negamus tamen optimum modum eligendi homines ad vitam aeternam esse illum, qui nititur praescientia meritorum. Non est optimus, quia non optime facit ad illustrandam gloriam purae misericordiae Divinae erga electos. Nam tollit illud quod Augustinus passim inculcat, Detur totum Deo. Tollit etiam illud Cypriani, ab Augustino nunquam satis laudatum, In nullo gloriandum; quia nihil est nostrum.
